FXUS06 KWBC 032027
PMDMRD
Prognostic Discussion for 6 to 10 and 8 to 14 day outlooks
NWS Climate Prediction Center College Park, MD
300 PM EST Tue November 03 2026

6-10 DAY OUTLOOK FOR NOV 09 - 13 2026

The 0Z ECMWF, GEFS, and Canadian ensemble mean forecasts are in fairly good 
agreement on the average large-scale circulation pattern over the North America 
domain during the 6-10 day period. While these ensemble mean 500-hPa height 
forecasts are generally similar, there are differences in the phase and 
amplitude of the primary features resulting in some differences in model 
temperature and precipitation forecasts. The manual height blend is based on 0Z 
ECMWF, GEFS, and Canadian model 500-hPa height forecasts, weighting the ECMWF 
ensemble mean greater due to recent model skill. The manual blend indicates a 
deep slow-moving trough over the Aleutians, southwestern Mainland Alaska, 
northeastern Pacific and off the West Coast of the contiguous United States 
(CONUS). Anomalous ridging with above normal heights is forecast over much of 
the western and central CONUS. Meanwhile a trough is forecast along the Eastern 
Seaboard. Below normal 500-hPa heights are forecast over the Aleutians, 
Mainland Alaska, and Southeast Alaska, while above normal mid-level heights are 
forecast across Hawaii near the eastern extension of a ridge forecast over the 
central Pacific. 

Above normal temperatures are likely across the West, due to anomalous ridging 
ahead of the deep trough forecast over the northeastern Pacific. As this ridge 
progresses eastward, an increasingly warm pattern is favored across the 
north-central CONUS, with probabilities of above normal temperatures exceeding 
80 percent across the Northern Rockies, the Northern Plains, and the Upper 
Mississippi Valley. Farther to the south and east, a trough predicted over the 
Eastern Seaboard reduces chances of anomalous warmth. Near normal temperatures 
are favored over most of the Eastern Seaboard and much of the Southeast 
associated with a trough predicted over the region, supported by most of the 
dynamical temperature forecast tools. Above normal temperatures are likely 
across much of eastern Alaska, ahead of the deep trough over the northeastern 
Pacific. Near to below normal temperatures are more likely from the Aleutians 
to the western Mainland Alaska, closer to the mean trough axis. Above normal 
temperatures are likely across Hawaii, mainly in response to observed above 
normal SSTs over much of the tropical Pacific, associated with the current El 
Nino.

The positioning and strength of the cyclonic flow over the northeast Pacific 
promotes an active pattern across much of the western and southwestern CONUS, 
eastern Mainland Alaska, and Southeast Alaska. Probabilities of above normal 
precipitation exceed 60 percent across northern and central portions of the 
West Coast. Above normal precipitation is also favored in parts of southern 
Florida, ahead of the mean trough position predicted over the region. Near to 
below normal precipitation is favored over the remainder of the CONUS, 
supported by most of the dynamical precipitation forecast tools. A slight tilt 
toward below normal precipitation is also indicated for parts of western 
Mainland Alaska, due to the predicted mean low level offshore flow. For Hawaii, 
near normal precipitation is favored for the Big Island, while below normal 
precipitation is slightly favored over Maui, Oahu, and Kauai, consistent with 
an automated blend. 

The official 6-10 day 500-hPa height blend consists of 30% of Today's 0z GFS 
Ensemble Mean centered on Day 8, 40% of Today's 0z European Ensemble Mean 
centered on Day 8, and 30% of Today's 0z Canadian Ensemble Mean centered on Day 
8 
 

FORECAST CONFIDENCE FOR THE 6-10 DAY PERIOD: Above average, 4 out of 5, due to 
fairly good agreement among today'smodel height solutions, offset by some 
differences among model temperature and precipitation tools. 

8-14 DAY OUTLOOK FOR NOV 11 - 17 2026 

The 0Z ECMWF, GEFS, and Canadian ensemble mean solutions for the 8Ã¢ÂÂ14 day 
period predict a fairly consistent 500-hPa circulation pattern relative to the 
6Ã¢ÂÂ10 day period across North America and the surrounding regions. ECMWF based 
tools were generally weighted more in the forecast, due to greater skill and 
persistence of yesterday's forecast. However, uncertainty increases in the 
forecasts for several areas of the domain. The 8-14 day manual blend 500-hPa 
height pattern shows a deep trough and negative 500-hPa height anomalies over 
the northeastern Pacific and the West Coast. Residual cyclonic flow is forecast 
in its wake over southwestern Alaska. Downstream ridging and above normal 
500-hPa heights are forecast over the north-central CONUS. Farther to the 
south, weak anomalous troughing and weak below normal 500-hPa heights are 
predicted over the southeastern CONUS. Above normal mid-level heights are 
forecast to continue across Hawaii, associated with broad ridging over the 
central Pacific.

Above normal temperatures are favored across the CONUS associated with 
anomalous ridging ahead of the deep trough over the northeastern Pacific. The 
highest confidence (greater than 80 percent chance) for anomalous warmth is 
indicated for parts of the Northern and Central Plains, and portions of the 
Upper Mississippi Valley as the ridge consolidates over the area throughout 
much of the period, supported by most of the dynamical temperature forecast 
tools. Anomalous warmth is favored across eastern Alaska, due to anomalous 
southeasterly low level flow ahead of a surface low predicted over the Gulf of 
Alaska. Near to below normal temperatures are favored behind this surface low, 
from the western Mainland to the Aleutians. Above normal temperatures are 
favored across Hawaii, underneath predicted above normal heights and consistent 
with expansive above normal SSTs associated with the current El Nino.

As the trough over the eastern Pacific slowly approaches the West coast, an 
active pattern is likely across much of the western and south-central CONUS as 
well as eastern Alaska. Probabilities of above normal precipitation exceed 50 
percent over most of California and parts of southwestern Nevada and western 
Arizona, where enhanced moisture flow is most likely. Above normal 
precipitation is modestly favored across parts of the Southeast, tied to a 
departing trough, supported by most of the dynamic precipitation forecast 
tools. Increased chances of near to below normal precipitation are favored 
across the remainder of the CONUS associated with ridging and above normal 
500-hPa heights. A tilt toward below normal precipitation is also indicated for 
parts of western Mainland Alaska, due to predicted low level offshore flow. 
Near to below normal precipitation is favored for Hawaii, consistent with an 
automated blend.  

The official 8-14 day 500-hPa height blend consists of: 30% of Today's 0z GFS 
Ensemble Mean centered on Day 11, 40% of Today's 0z European Ensemble Mean 
centered on Day 11, and 30% of Today's 0z Canadian Ensemble Mean centered on 
Day 11 


FORECAST CONFIDENCE FOR THE 8-14 DAY PERIOD: Above average, 4 out of 5, due to 
fairly good agreement among today's model height solutions, offset by some 
differences among model temperature and precipitation tools. 


FORECASTER: Luke H

Notes:


The notation for the categorical forecast indicated on the maps is 
the same as that in the tables: A-above   N-near normal   B-below 
 
The temperature map shows regions with > 33% chance of being warmer
(orange, "A"), colder (blue, "B"), or close to (gray, "N") normal.
Labels on the shaded lines give the probability (> 33%) of the more
likely category (B or A). Probability of N is always < 40%.
 
The precipitation map shows regions with > 33% chance of being 
wetter (green, "A"), drier (tan, "B"), or close to (gray, "N")
normal. Labels on the shaded lines give the probability (> 33%) of
the more likely category (B or A). Probability of N is always < 40%.
 
In the southwest and other climatologically dry regions - there will 
be a greater than 33.3% chance of no precipitation and occasionally 
even a normal (i.e. Median) value of zero - especially during the dry 
seasons.  In such cases a forecast of near normal is effectively a 
forecast of little or no precipitation. 
 
The climate prediction center uses 1991-2020 base period means as  
reference in the climate outlooks.

The next set of long-lead monthly and seasonal outlooks will be released on 
November 19.


Analogs to the 5 day mean observed pattern centered 3 days ago (D-3)
for the region from 20N to 70N latitude and 175E to 60W longitude
include the 5 day periods centered on the following dates:
20161029 - 20221110 - 20001014 - 20081102 - 20001024


Analogs to the 7 day mean observed pattern centered 4 days ago (D-4)
for the region from 20N to 70N latitude and 175E to 60W longitude
include the 7 day periods centered on the following dates:
20221110 - 20161028 - 20001027 - 20081103 - 20151107
